In extreme-edge AI deployments, high-dimensional continuous input data—such as high-resolution image pixel arrays, dense audio waveforms, or natural language embeddings—must be aggressively compressed into lower-dimensional discrete representations prior to processing.1 The baseline QMINIWASM framework utilizes Ternary Locality-Sensitive Hashing (TLSH) to map these continuous values into discrete hashes while preserving critical topological distance metrics, such as Cosine similarity.1 The integration of Clifford entanglement significantly enhances this dimensionality reduction through a sophisticated technique inspired by Classical Shadow Tomography and Entanglement Cooling.24

In complex data embeddings, features inherently exhibit dense, long-range correlations that are computationally exhausting to process in real-time. Clifford circuits serve as a highly efficient hybrid component within tensor network frameworks to drastically reduce this computational complexity.24 By applying sequences of random qutrit Clifford unitaries directly to the input data streams, the framework subjects the input to "entanglement cooling".24 This systematic, iterative process utilizes Clifford transformations to strip away burdensome long-range correlations from the target state.24

The cooling strategy intentionally leaves behind a "residual state" that possesses substantially lower entanglement, making it mathematically much simpler and highly compressible for the TLSH algorithms.24 Because the Gottesman-Knill theorem guarantees that highly entangled stabilizer states remain classically tractable regardless of their initial entanglement depth, this intricate preprocessing step incurs only ![][image3] computational overhead, making it perfectly viable for edge execution.24

However, this sophisticated technique features a strict, mathematically proven boundary. Exhaustive studies establish that perfect Clifford disentangling is only achievable if the state maintains a specific factorized structure.24 It is formally proven that no sequence of Clifford operations can universally disentangle an arbitrary non-Clifford rotation.24 Therefore, the QMINIWASM framework must strictly constrain the input quantization to the ![][image2] basis states prior to applying the shadow protocols. ## **Domain 9: Forward-Forward Learning Optimization via Entanglement Entropy**

Because the entire architecture operates strictly over the Galois Field ![][image2] without the inclusion of any Floating-Point Units, traditional gradient descent via backpropagation is mathematically and physically impossible.1 The chain rule cannot be applied to discrete stabilizer tableaus. Instead, the framework successfully integrates the Forward-Forward (FF) algorithm, optimizing the neural network layer-by-layer using strictly consecutive forward execution passes.1 In standard classical FF applications, the network is trained to maximize a heuristic "goodness" metric (usually the sum of squared neuron activations) for positive data and minimize it for negative data.33

In the highly advanced, Clifford-enhanced QMINIWASM model, this goodness metric is completely redefined using the fundamental principles of **Entanglement Entropy** and stabilizer state overlap.32 In quantum statistical mechanics, entanglement entropy rigorously quantifies the degree of correlation between specific subsystems.35 In the context of the Clifford random tensor networks executing the AI routing, maximizing "goodness" corresponds directly to driving the subsystem toward a defined stabilizer state with exceptionally low entanglement entropy relative to the correct classification label.35

During the first forward pass, positive, ground-truth training samples are encoded into the qutrit tableau via Absmean quantization.1 The NAND CIM array executes the Clifford layers, and the WAVM calculates the localized entanglement entropy by inspecting the mathematical rank of the resulting stabilizer subgroup.35 The ternary weights are subsequently adjusted via highly localized Hebbian-like updates to minimize this entropy, tightly binding the input feature topological structures to the correct expert routing paths within the MoE framework.35

During the second forward pass, negative samples (or artificially corrupted data) are fed through the network.33 The update rules are strictly inverted to actively maximize the entanglement entropy, effectively pushing the stabilizer tableau into a highly disordered, chaotic state when presented with incorrect or out-of-distribution information.33 This aggressive stochastic drift away from the uniform codespace provides a stark, easily measurable contrast between correct and incorrect classifications without ever requiring any chain-rule derivatives or floating-point gradients to be calculated.32

By utilizing entanglement entropy as the localized loss function, the Forward-Forward algorithm perfectly aligns with the non-contextual, tracking-based mechanics of the Gottesman-Knill theorem. The WAVM only needs to monitor the structural rank of the ![][image11] matrix to execute highly accurate learning, resulting in an exceptionally low-overhead training regimen perfectly suitable for continual, autonomous, on-device learning at the extreme edge.
